cards.title: Define the customer before designing the experience
cards.claim: Before deciding what the customer experience should be, you first have to decide who your customer is and what you do for them, including deeper motivators, attitudes, values, and purposes.
cards.action: Define who your customer is and what you do for them before deciding the experience, and seek to understand their key motivators, attitudes toward products/services, values in business relationships, personal purposes, and how your organization makes them feel.
applies_when: Designing or deciding what a customer experience should be
unknowns: No specific method for assessing customer motivators, attitudes, values, personal purposes, or feelings is provided in the passage.
evidence_quotes: before deciding this whole thing with experience what the experience should be you first have to decide who is your customer and what do you do for them

do you know their key motivators not just with your product or your service but the key motivators for them do you know their attitudes towards your products and services do you know what they value in a relationship in business do you know what personal purposes they have and is your organization set up to really understand the way that you are making your customers feel

cards.title: Create a customer strategy as an umbrella for the organization
cards.claim: A customer strategy should define the desired customer experience and what you want customers to feel across the journey, and include customer principles and practical translation.
cards.action: Put a customer strategy umbrella over the organization that states the CX experience you want customers to feel, the customer principles you live by, what that translates into in practice, and actions to make it really happen.
applies_when: Building or managing customer experience strategy
Aligning business purpose, objectives, and strategy with customer experience
do_not_use_when: When the customer strategy is only about which segments you're going for or what areas you're penetrating
unknowns: The passage does not specify how to create or operationalize the customer strategy.
evidence_quotes: a customer strategy it's like this umbrella over the whole organization that everything you do is towards what you want your customers to really feel

a customer strategy includes things like what our customer strategy is I mean the CX the experience what we want our customers to feel what are the customers principles we live by and what does that translate to into practice

I'm not talking about the customer strategy that says which segments you're going for or what areas you're penetrating and so forth I'm talking about what you have decided that the experience should be what you want your customers to feel in the whole journey they have with you

cards.title: Use customer journey mapping to design and manage CX
cards.claim: Customer journey mapping is a tool to design and manage the whole experience, understand the customer's experience, create a realistic view of the journey, and see where to focus for customers and business results; customers experience a journey, not processes.
cards.action: Use customer journey mapping to design and manage the whole experience, understand the customer's experience, create a realistic view of the journey, identify where to focus for customers and business results, and assess how capable business processes are to deliver the customer journey.
applies_when: Designing or managing the customer experience
Assessing business process capability to deliver the customer journey
do_not_use_when: When the thing cannot be felt, heard, seen, or touched—the passage says it is a process, not a journey
unknowns: The passage does not provide a step-by-step journey mapping method or metrics.
evidence_quotes: customer journey mapping is a tool to be able to answer that question and not only that it's the most powerful tool to design and manage the whole experience
by mapping this customer journey you get an outside and understanding of the experience they have it will help you to create this realistic view of the journey
customers don't experience processes they experience a journey if they cannot feel it hear it see it touch it it is not a journey it is a process
mapping this will also help you to ship see where you should put your focus where it matters most to your customers and to your business results of course
how capable are your business processes right now in delivering your customer journey
